question: SQ-LIP-000025
text: What specific genetic variants or inheritance patterns have been identified in lipedema?
minor_problems: [minor] set: Tension between P2 (autosomal dominant inheritance most consistent) and the polygenic/heterogeneous architecture in E2, E11 and E12 and the no-single-gene statement in P3; no proposition states the polygenic model explicitly.
[minor] set: E18 (narrative review of AKR1C variants) re-reports E19 without secondary_of, and E11 re-reports E4, E12, E14 and E19 (used only for family history, acceptable).
[minor] set: E16 (systematic review: no confirmed gene, syndromic associations) supports P3 but is filed only under P2; syndromic gene associations (POU1F1, NSD1, ELN) have no proposition.

[minor] P1: two ideas — suggested: A positive family history is commonly reported in people with lipedema, with estimates varying widely and affected relatives mostly female. (Frequency rests on E21 (46%) and a review (E11, 30-89%); E9 (14.9% with an affected first-degree relative) and E16 (up to 64%), placed under P2, show how widely it varies. Bundles frequency with the sex of relatives, which only E21 (and E9) support.)

[minor] P2: not fully supported; overgeneralized; two ideas — suggested: Small pedigree series and reviews suggest autosomal dominant inheritance with sex limitation, although heterogeneous or polygenic contributions are also reported. (Primary support is one pedigree series (E9) and a brief description in E24; E16, E10 and E17 are reviews restating it. 'Reduced penetrance in males' is stated only in E24 (and 'incomplete penetrance' in E16). Items E2, E11 and E12 point to heterogeneous/polygenic architecture, which conflicts with an unqualified 'most consistent with autosomal dominant'.)

[minor] P3: two ideas; misplaced ['E15'] (Supported by E2 (no gene shared across 9 families) and by E16/E24 (no confirmed gene), but E16 and E24 sit under P2. E15 (estrogen signalling and sex-hormone gene variants) does not bear on whether a single gene exists. Statement is in mild tension with P4/E7 ('first mutated gene').)

[minor] P5: not fully supported; overgeneralized — suggested: Common variants at several loci are associated with a lipedema-like phenotype in genome-wide studies, though samples are small and replication is limited. ('Linked to body fat distribution' is not stated in any finding; E13/E14 loci relate to lipoma formation and hormone biosynthesis. E12 uses an inferred phenotype in a biobank rather than clinically diagnosed lipedema, and E14 is only suggestive (not genome-wide significant, n=130). E13 is the preprint of E14, correctly marked secondary.)

[minor] P6: overgeneralized — suggested: Rare predicted-deleterious variants in genes of lipid metabolism and insulin signalling are reported in a minority of people with lipedema. (Single uncontrolled panel study (E4), E5 is a secondary citation. Stated as established fact; no control or replication, and several listed genes (POMC, RYR1, GHR) are not clearly lipid or adipogenesis genes.)

[minor] P7: not fully supported (One small case-control study, wide confidence interval (1.98-17.71), no replication; the quoted passage concerns body-composition indices, with the OR only in old_statement. Hedged with 'may', so acceptable.)

old_statements: In a case-control study, carriers of the IL-6 rs1800795 G allele had a 5.92-fold higher risk of lipedema (OR=5.92, 95%CI 1.983–17.711, p<0.001), and DXA-derived body composition indices (reduced WHR 0.73 vs 0.79, higher lower-limb FM% 48.90% vs 42.55%) combined with genetic analysis were proposed as tools for differential diagnosis between lipedema, normal-weight obesity, and obesity.

items.title: A Family-Based Study of Inherited Genetic Risk in Lipedema
items.quote: Historical evaluation of individuals with lipedema indicates a positive family history in 60%-80% of cases; however, genetic investigation of larger family cohorts is required.
items.note: The article directly addresses the question by reporting specific candidate genes/pathways and inheritance patterns; it refines the affirmative by concluding lipedema shows polygenic heterogeneity rather than a single Mendelian variant.
old_statements: Family-based exome sequencing of 31 individuals from 9 lipedema families identified candidate variants in 469 genes with no single gene shared across all families, supporting genetic heterogeneity rather than a Mendelian single-gene cause, with gene ontology enrichment in vasopressin receptor activity (AVPR1A, AVPR2), microfibril binding (FBN, ELN, LTBP), and patched binding (PTCH1/2, Hedgehog pathway).

Review cites 21 deleterious variants in 12 genes identified in 17 of 162 lipedema patients.

propositions.statement: A polymorphism in the interleukin-six gene may be associated with increased lipedema risk.
propositions.rationale: A single case-control study reports an association with an inflammatory gene polymorphism; it is hedged pending replication.

evidence.finding: Carriers of the IL-6 rs1800795 G allele had higher lipedema risk (OR 5.92, 95% CI 1.98-17.71, p<0.001).

propositions.statement: Lipedema adipose tissue and stem cells show altered gene expression and DNA methylation compared with controls.
propositions.rationale: Expression and methylation differences describe tissue biology rather than identifying inherited variants or transmission patterns.

evidence.finding: Systematic review notes 3429 differentially expressed genes in lipedema adipose-derived stem cells, including cell-cycle genes; aetiology uncertain and no inherited variants identified.
Adipogenesis PCR array of 84 genes: CCND1 upregulated (2.16x) and CEBPD, CFD, NCOR2, KLF4 downregulated in lipedema tissue vs matched controls.
In late-stage lipedema, over 5000 differentially methylated CpG sites and AKT1 promoter hypomethylation correlating with increased AKT1 expression and phosphorylation.

dropped.reason: Not a finding: nutritional scoping review only mentions genetic predisposition without any variant or inheritance result.

verdicts.suggested_statement: A positive family history is commonly reported in people with lipedema, with estimates varying widely and affected relatives mostly female.
verdicts.note: Frequency rests on E21 (46%) and a review (E11, 30-89%); E9 (14.9% with an affected first-degree relative) and E16 (up to 64%), placed under P2, show how widely it varies. Bundles frequency with the sex of relatives, which only E21 (and E9) support.

verdicts.suggested_statement: Small pedigree series and reviews suggest autosomal dominant inheritance with sex limitation, although heterogeneous or polygenic contributions are also reported.
verdicts.note: Primary support is one pedigree series (E9) and a brief description in E24; E16, E10 and E17 are reviews restating it. 'Reduced penetrance in males' is stated only in E24 (and 'incomplete penetrance' in E16). Items E2, E11 and E12 point to heterogeneous/polygenic architecture, which conflicts with an unqualified 'most consistent with autosomal dominant'.

Supported by E2 (no gene shared across 9 families) and by E16/E24 (no confirmed gene), but E16 and E24 sit under P2. E15 (estrogen signalling and sex-hormone gene variants) does not bear on whether a single gene exists. Statement is in mild tension with P4/E7 ('first mutated gene').

verdicts.suggested_statement: Missense variants in the progesterone-metabolising enzyme gene AKR1C1 have been reported in a lipedema family and in patients and are proposed as a cause of familial lipedema.
verdicts.note: Hedged by 'proposed'. Evidence is one three-affected family (E19, segregation only), a computational/targeted study without a family design (E20) and a review (E18) that re-reports E19 without secondary_of. 'An aldo-keto reductase gene' is vaguer than the evidence, which is mostly AKR1C1.

verdicts.suggested_statement: Common variants at several loci are associated with a lipedema-like phenotype in genome-wide studies, though samples are small and replication is limited.
verdicts.note: 'Linked to body fat distribution' is not stated in any finding; E13/E14 loci relate to lipoma formation and hormone biosynthesis. E12 uses an inferred phenotype in a biobank rather than clinically diagnosed lipedema, and E14 is only suggestive (not genome-wide significant, n=130). E13 is the preprint of E14, correctly marked secondary.

verdicts.suggested_statement: Rare predicted-deleterious variants in genes of lipid metabolism and insulin signalling are reported in a minority of people with lipedema.
verdicts.note: Single uncontrolled panel study (E4), E5 is a secondary citation. Stated as established fact; no control or replication, and several listed genes (POMC, RYR1, GHR) are not clearly lipid or adipogenesis genes.

One small case-control study, wide confidence interval (1.98-17.71), no replication; the quoted passage concerns body-composition indices, with the OR only in old_statement. Hedged with 'may', so acceptable.
Context proposition; E8 is a review of expression findings (Ishaq), E22 and E23 are primary. Not about inherited variants, as the findings themselves say.

set_issues.issue: Tension between P2 (autosomal dominant inheritance most consistent) and the polygenic/heterogeneous architecture in E2, E11 and E12 and the no-single-gene statement in P3; no proposition states the polygenic model explicitly.
E18 (narrative review of AKR1C variants) re-reports E19 without secondary_of, and E11 re-reports E4, E12, E14 and E19 (used only for family history, acceptable).
E16 (systematic review: no confirmed gene, syndromic associations) supports P3 but is filed only under P2; syndromic gene associations (POU1F1, NSD1, ELN) have no proposition.
